slides.title: Cracks and speed breakers ruining your session?
slides.sub: Rough road skating is a skill you can learn

slides.title: Lift your eyes
slides.body: Pick your line 15 to 20 metres ahead and commit at 5 to 8 metres. Most skaters look at their own wheels, and every hazard arrives with no time attached.

slides.title: Cross cracks close to square
slides.caption: Met at a shallow angle, a crack swallows the wheel and steers it. Met close to square, it is a short bump.

slides.title: Unweight over speed breakers
slides.body: Stay low on the approach, let your hips float up as the front wheel reaches the hump, then settle and push once both skates are past.

slides.title: Gravel and wet patches
slides.body: Go around if you safely can. If not, cross in a straight line with no push, no lean and no steering. Most slips come from steering mid patch.

slides.text: Step over, unweight, or change the angle.

slides.title: Let your setup help
slides.body: A softer compound soaks up the buzz and a bigger diameter bridges more of every gap. Keep your bearings clean, because rough roads fill them with grit.
